All food sold in Australia and New Zealand must comply with food standards. These standards are compiled in the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code. FSANZ assesses applications to amend the Code and prepares proposals to vary existing standards or develop new ones.

## What you need to know

## Prohibited and restricted items

To protect our people, environment, and economy, some goods:

* require a permit
* must be declared
* aren’t allowed into the country at all.

Here you’ll find information on the rules for:

* medicines
* food, plants, animal products, and other risk items
* weapons
* commercial goods
* other items you might be travelling with.

### What prohibited means

Prohibited items are not allowed into New Zealand under any circumstances. These items pose a significant risk to our biosecurity, public health, or national security.

You must declare any prohibited items when you arrive in New Zealand.

Bringing in prohibited items is a serious offence and can lead to your arrest.

### What restricted means

You need a permit or an exemption to bring these items into New Zealand.

## Specific rules for what you're bringing into New Zealand

Checking these requirements before you travel will help you:

* avoid delays
* ensure compliance with Customs and biosecurity regulations
* make your arrival as smooth as possible.

If in doubt, declare it!

### Medicines

Prescription medicines and controlled drugs (medicines and drugs with strict regulations) have specific requirements. These must be declared on your New Zealand Traveller Declaration.

#### Prescription medicines

If you are arriving in New Zealand with prescription medicines (that do not contain controlled drugs), you must:

* bring a copy of your prescription, or a letter from your doctor confirming you are being treated with the medicine
* keep the medicine in its original packaging
* bring no more than three months of supply
  + You may bring up to six months of supply if the medicine is an oral contraceptive.

##### When to declare prescription medicine

You must declare your prescription medicine if either of the following apply:

* you are carrying more than three months of supply
* the medicine is not prescribed to you or a family member.

Learn more about bringing medicines into New Zealand on Medsafe - this includes guidance on non-prescription medicines.

#### Controlled drugs - Declare

Controlled drugs are medicines or drugs with strict regulations. If you are arriving in New Zealand with controlled drugs, you must:

* declare the controlled drugs on your New Zealand Traveller Declaration
* keep the controlled drugs in their original packaging
* bring no more than one month of supply.
* bring either of the following:
  + a copy of your prescription
  + a letter from your doctor confirming both of these:
    - you are being treated with the controlled drugs
    - the name and strength of these drugs

All controlled drugs must be declared on your New Zealand Traveller Declaration.

Find out more about controlled drugs at Ministry of Health

#### Pseudoephedrine - Declare

All medicines containing pseudoephedrine are controlled drugs. If you are arriving in New Zealand with medicine containing pseudoephedrine, you must:

* follow all the controlled drugs declaration instructions
* keep the medicine with you in your hand luggage.

You cannot bring medicines with pseudoephedrine into New Zealand for friends or family.
